newsitem.title: USA: U.S. files discrimination complaint against Ford.
newsitem.headline: U.S. files discrimination complaint against Ford.

text.p: The Labor Department has filed a complaint against Ford Motor Co., alleging the company discriminated against women who applied for jobs at its Louisville, Kent., assembly plant in 1993, the department announced Wednesday.

The complaint says Ford discriminated against female applicants in its hiring and selection procedures for entry-level laborer positions at the plant. It also says Ford failed to cooperate with a government probe when the company denied investigators access to information they thought was relevant to the case, the Labor Department said.
The Labor Department is asking Ford to compensate the affected group of women by providing employment, lost wages, interest and other job benefits, the department said.

The complaint is a result of a compliance review conducted by the department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs beginning in May 1993. Ford was served the complaint on March 31 this year, the department said.

The OFCCP enforces laws that prohibit job discrimination among federal contractors. Ford's Louisville assembly plant, which makes trucks, is considered a federal contractor since it sells some of the trucks it makes to the U.S. government.
